sourceChecks.title: Observation of robust macroscale structural superlubricity
sourceChecks.excerpt: friction coefficients that fluctuate around zero
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Authors report macroscale structural superlubricity in a sub-millimeter graphite contact, reaching coefficients as low as 10^-6 over 1 mN–0.5 N.
sourceChecks.limitations: Single flat layered-material contact and stated load range; does not establish dry ambient MPa contact, m/s sliding, indefinite wear-free operation, or machine-wide energy savings.

sourceChecks.title: Computer Simulation/Prediction of Wear in Mechanical Components
sourceChecks.excerpt: wear models, contact analysis schemes, and wear evolution prediction procedures
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The review describes computational wear-prediction models for selected mechanical components and summarizes model families and contact-analysis methods.
sourceChecks.limitations: Reviewed models depend on component, mechanism and operating conditions; it does not establish a universal first-principles model with exact forecasts for any pair/environment or guaranteed lifetime.

sourceChecks.title: Deep generative model-based synthesis framework of four-bar linkage mechanisms with target conditions
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A conditional generative model proposes four-bar linkages for specified kinematic and quasi-static target conditions.
sourceChecks.limitations: The scope is four-bar linkage synthesis; the paper notes imperfect target paths, data limitations, and does not solve arbitrary multi-body path/timing/force/dynamics requirements with zero error.

sourceChecks.title: Energy Storage Technology and Cost Characterization Report
sourceChecks.paraphrase: DOE report summarizes flywheel estimates including 70–90% RTE for several systems and expected lifetimes around 20 years; one vendor estimate reaches 98%.
sourceChecks.limitations: Estimates vary by system/source and are not zero-loss storage; they do not establish zero measurable losses over years or a scalable universal system.

sourceChecks.paraphrase: A targeted search located a potentially relevant paper on stress-induced self-healing in a molecular crystal, but the Nature page redirected to an inaccessible identity-protection page.
sourceChecks.limitations: The content could not be read; search-result information is not treated as positive evidence.

sourceChecks.title: Experimental and numerical investigation on effects of viscoelastic rubber and local resonator mass on broadband vibration attenuation in acoustic-metamaterial plates
sourceChecks.excerpt: over a frequency range of 8−4000 Hz
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Experimental plate tests and numerical analysis found acoustic-metamaterial attenuation regions over an 8–4000 Hz response range.
sourceChecks.limitations: This plate-scale frequency-specific result does not establish 100% attenuation, DC–MHz coverage, all six degrees of freedom, or engineering-scale loads.

sourceChecks.title: Improving propulsive efficiency using bio-inspired intermittent locomotion
sourceChecks.excerpt: saving up to 24% of the energy
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A model-scale boat with a folding propeller saved up to 24% energy in tested burst-and-coast conditions.
sourceChecks.limitations: This does not establish 90% propulsive efficiency, comparative biological parity, low-noise/cavitation-free performance, or an arbitrary scalable propulsor.

sourceChecks.title: The role of adhesion in contact mechanics
sourceChecks.excerpt: strengths and limitations of various methods
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The review surveys analytical methods for adhesive contact, including experimental measurements and effects of surface roughness, with explicit attention to limits of methods.
sourceChecks.limitations: It does not supply one closed-form theory that predicts all adhesion, friction, hysteresis and deformation for arbitrary surfaces, environments and loads.

sourceChecks.title: SHAFT: A Slack-Compensating, Helical-Buckling-Attenuating Flexible-Shaft Transmission for Lightweight Multi-DoF Manipulation
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A flexible-shaft transmission with a proximal tensioner showed about 30% higher efficiency and 65% lower angular transmission error than an untensioned shaft in a path with four 90-degree bends.
sourceChecks.limitations: It is not lossless, has residual angular transmission error, and tests a specific robot mechanism/path rather than arbitrary distances and curvatures.

sourceChecks.title: Flexible multibody modelling for exact constraint design of compliant mechanisms
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A finite-element multibody method analyzes degrees of freedom and visualizes overconstraint stress distributions in a straight-guiding compliant mechanism example.
sourceChecks.limitations: This provides analysis/design tools; it does not establish massively overconstrained mechanisms moving freely with zero internal stress at any scale.
